title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
description: Sunlight is white, so why does the sky look blue? It comes down to tiny air molecules. #science #physics #shorts

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sky isn't actually painted blue. So why does it look that way?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sunlight looks white, but it's really every color mixed together.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When it hits our atmosphere, it crashes into tiny gas molecules.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Those molecules scatter short wavelengths, like blue, far more than red.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So blue light bounces all over the sky and reaches your eyes from every direction.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At sunset, light travels through much more air before reaching you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most of the blue gets scattered away, leaving reds and oranges.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This effect is called Rayleigh scattering.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So every blue sky is really just sunlight bouncing off air.
